newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - BPB sees further hit by stg.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - BPB sees further hit by stg.

text.p: British building materials company BPB Industries Plc said on Thursday that it would be able to beat a sluggish industry for marginal growth but would continue to be hit by a strengthening sterling in the current financial year.
"We have been hit by three million sterling in the first six months. It could go up to 10 to 15 million stg for the full year," BPB's managing director Jean-Pierre Cuny told Reuters in an interview.

Sterling, currently trading at around 2.56 Deutsche marks, is at its highest levels since February 1994. The company on Thursday reported a higher pre-tax profit in its first six months to September 30 of 106.7 million stg, compared with 83.6 milliion in the previous year.

However, BPB expressed caution that the continuous rise in sterling against the German mark and the French franc, combined with a slow-moving housing market in those two countries, could stem further optimism.

Cuny said the company's overall volume growth for the whole 1996/97 would be at around four percent, higher than two percent in the previous year. "...But a strong market for our technology and stable higher prices should make us feel better than competition," he said.

Most British building materials manufacturers have been hit recently by rising sterling and curb in government expenditures in Germany and France as they try to conform to stringent EMU conditions as part of the Maastricht treaty.
Cuny said the German building industry had now bottomed out.
He said he expected the industry in that country to hit the growth path by early 1997.
The company is already expanding the capacity of its plant in Vetschau, most of which will be devoted to make plaster and gypsum floorscreeds.
Cuny said that unlike most traditional building materials manufacturer, BPB was in a niche market given the type of its product.
"The plasterboards are cheap, easy to handle and are also finding markets in other places," he said.
BPB plans to invest about 50 million stg in Poland and Czech Republic where it hopes to start operations in three years.
The company's new plant in Cape Town, South Africa is expected to start operations in mid-1997, he said. BPB recently took control of its South African subsidiary at a cost of 39.8 million stg.
BPB also has plans to invest about 21 million in the UK and Ireland in the current financial year.
"We had plans of 130 million stg capital investments for 1996/97. We have done 50 in the first half," he said.
Jean-Pierre said he expected a fair amount of growth coming from North America, especially Canada where housing and renovation segments were responding to an emergence out of recession.
He said despite its expansions, the company had no plans to raise fresh funds.
"We are cash-rich. We would also maintain our progressive dividend policy," he said.
